items.prompt: In a fraud review system, a risk analyst must place a case into review. high-risk cases must not be silently dropped while low-value work is constrained The design review focuses on threat modeling, secure defaults, and security trade-offs. constraints: high-risk cases must not be silently dropped while low-value work is constrained
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is threat-model trust boundaries and make the safe behavior the default when evidence is missing..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Threat-model trust boundaries and make the safe behavior the default when evidence is missing. In this normal path for fraud review, security constraints change api, data, network, tenancy, and operations decisions together. The owner must also make overload in the review queue observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide threat modeling, secure defaults, and security trade-offs independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat overload in the review queue as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Threat-model trust boundaries and make the safe behavior the default when evidence is missing. It addresses high-risk cases must not be silently dropped while low-value work is constrained through an explicit mechanism and keeps overload in the review queue inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Threat modeling, secure defaults, and security trade-offs” to terminology recall. Authentication is not authorization, encryption is not isolation, and client-side controls are not enforcement; define explicit trust boundaries.
